articles.title: Lindsey Vonn dodges red carpet wardrobe mishap ahead of another surgery
articles.standfirst: The Olympic skiing icon handled an unexpected fashion scare with the same composure she has shown throughout a difficult recovery from her devastating Cortina crash
articles.summary: The Olympic skiing icon handled an unexpected fashion scare with the same composure she has shown throughout a difficult recovery from her devastating Cortina crash
articles.body:
Lindsey Vonn has spent decades mastering the art of staying upright when everything around her is moving at extraordinary speed. That instinct came in handy again this week, although this time there were no skis, gates or downhill course involved.

The 41-year-old Olympic champion attended the Kering Foundation's Caring for Women Dinner in New York City on Thursday, September 10, turning heads in an elegant red gown featuring a dramatic cape.

The outfit made for an eye-catching appearance as Vonn posed for photographers, with gold jewelry, white heels and a black clutch completing the look. Her blonde hair was worn in loose waves over one shoulder.

But while attempting to adjust the cape for the cameras, Vonn was briefly faced with an unexpected problem. The movement caused one of the gown's straps to slip from her shoulder.

Rather than allowing the moment to become an embarrassing red-carpet incident, Vonn quickly corrected the dress and carried on posing.

The brief mishap was hardly the biggest challenge she has faced this year.

Vonn's appearance came as she continues to work through an extraordinarily difficult rehabilitation following her crash at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Cortina d'Ampezzo.

The skier suffered a devastating complex fracture to her left tibia after crashing only 13 seconds into the Olympic downhill. She has undergone five surgeries since the accident, with another operation still ahead.

Another operation remains part of Vonn's long recovery

The next stage of Vonn's rehabilitation involves surgery on the ACL she tore shortly before the Olympics.

Vonn suffered the ligament injury during a World Cup race in Switzerland on January 30. Rather than abandon her Olympic dream, she decided to compete in Cortina despite the torn ACL.

Her subsequent downhill crash dramatically changed the situation, leaving her with a serious tibia injury that required multiple procedures to stabilize her leg.

The fact that Vonn still has to address the ACL injury illustrates just how complicated her recovery has become.

Speaking with TNT Sports at the US Open on August 30, Vonn acknowledged that another significant stage of rehabilitation awaits her.

'So, I'm trying to get as strong as possible, and once I get my ACL, then I'll have another long road ahead of me, but for now I feel great, and I'm very thankful for that,' she added.

Vonn has previously indicated that she hopes to undergo the ACL operation in November. Reuters reported that she expects roughly nine months of recovery after that procedure, meaning her focus is currently firmly on rebuilding her body rather than deciding whether she will race again.

That uncertainty has surrounded Vonn since the Olympic crash.

The former World Cup champion has not committed to another competitive skiing comeback, and she has acknowledged that retirement remains a possibility. For now, however, she appears more interested in judging her recovery one step at a time rather than looking too far into the future.

That approach is understandable given how much her physical condition has changed since February.

Vonn has described the months since the Olympics as being dominated by rehabilitation. At the same time, she has celebrated small improvements that would have seemed insignificant before the accident but now represent important milestones.

She recently told People that her summer had consisted of 'a lot of rehab' and 'a lot of recovery.'

'But I'm finally doing better,' she told the outlet. 'I was able to play tennis yesterday and that was a really big day for me. So it's coming along, slowly but surely.'

The return to tennis was particularly notable because Vonn previously revealed that even walking remained difficult during the early stages of her rehabilitation.

At the 2026 ESPYs in July, she explained that she had spent significant time using a wheelchair and crutches and had struggled to return to meaningful gym work. Her progress since then has offered some encouragement.

The former Olympic downhill champion has already demonstrated that she can recover from setbacks that would end most athletes' careers. Her return to elite competition itself was remarkable: after retiring in 2019, Vonn returned to World Cup skiing and eventually earned her place at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

She then arrived at those Games carrying an ACL injury and attempted to compete before the downhill crash brought her season to an abrupt end.

Now, the objective is considerably simpler: getting healthy.

The Kering Foundation event therefore provided a snapshot of a different side of Vonn . Away from the slopes and rehabilitation room, she was able to attend a major New York event and confidently navigate the red carpet.

The wardrobe scare lasted only a moment, but Vonn's response was fitting. She fixed the problem, carried on and kept smiling. Her next challenge will be much more demanding.

With another operation approaching and months of rehabilitation likely to follow, Vonn still has a long road ahead.

But after five surgeries, months of recovery and an injury that came dangerously close to ending her season, and potentially much more, the fact that she is once again enjoying activities such as tennis and appearing at major public events represents meaningful progress.

Whether she ultimately returns to competitive skiing remains unknown.

For now, Vonn appears content to concentrate on the next milestone, with her upcoming ACL surgery likely to be the next major test in one of the most remarkable recovery stories of her career.

articles.title: Simone Biles' busy life with Jonathan Owens puts her return to the Los Angeles Olympics in doubt
articles.standfirst: The gymnastics superstar has been enjoying trips, fashion and time with loved ones
articles.summary: The gymnastics superstar has been enjoying trips, fashion and time with loved ones
articles.body:
S imone Biles has spent much of the past few weeks giving fans glimpses into a life that looks very different from the demanding routine of an Olympic gymnast.

From international trips and designer outfits to game days with her husband, Jonathan Owens , and time with friends and family, the 11-time Olympic medalist appears to be making the most of life outside elite competition.

That does not necessarily mean Biles has abandoned the possibility of returning to gymnastics.

However, with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics approaching and her comeback plans still undecided, the contrast between her visible lifestyle and the relatively limited training content she has shared publicly has become difficult to ignore.

One of her most recent high-profile appearances came in London, where she travelled to support Owens as the Indianapolis Colts faced the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 4.

Biles shared glimpses of her day with followers, including time with her friend Torrie Brown, her journey to the stadium and a carefully planned outfit inspired by the British capital.

Fashion was a major part of the appearance. Biles wore a custom two-piece trench-style outfit featuring Owens ' number and surname, alongside jewellery and a sparkling Chanel bag.

The trip followed another Colts game the previous week, when she coordinated designer looks with Owens and shared photos with friends and family.

These moments offer a glimpse into the interests and relationships occupying her time away from the gym. But they also raise a question that will follow Biles as the next Olympics draw closer: how much does she genuinely want to commit to another demanding Olympic cycle?

Travel, fashion and family life are taking centre stage

Biles has previously spoken about the difficulty of balancing her own career with Owens' NFL schedule.

In September, she told Us Weekly that she would not normally travel to his away games during the 2026 season, explaining that she wanted to use those weekends to work on her own commitments after attending every game the previous year.

She nevertheless made the trip to London for the Colts ' international fixture.

Her public updates have also highlighted fashion, social occasions and the time she spends supporting her husband.

Those posts do not establish how often she trains privately, and a lack of gym videos should not be mistaken for proof that she is doing no preparation. Still, fans have far more visible evidence of her activities outside gymnastics than of a structured build-up towards LA28.

Biles has been candid that she has not made a final decision about competing again. Speaking on Good Morning America, she explained why the opportunity to compete on home soil is appealing but said she still needs to weigh the personal costs.

“I feel like it’s hard to turn down home Games, but at the end of the day, I need to weigh the present cons of what it’s really going to look like. So, I have to be really confident in that decision. So, I still say 50-50. I did see my coaches the other day, and we always talk about it and what that journey would look like, and I’ve been in the gym, like flipping around and seeing what the air awareness looks like. So, it’s fun to go and flip,” she said.

That update confirms she has been back in the gym experimenting with skills, even if she has not publicly outlined a full training programme.

Her comments suggest the door remains open, but a few sessions are a long way from committing to the years of preparation required to contend for Olympic medals.

Family plans are another important consideration. Biles and Owens have spoken about wanting to start a family, and another Olympic campaign would require considerable time, travel and sacrifice.

At 29, with an extraordinary career already behind her, Biles has reasons to consider whether another Games would fit the life she wants next.

She has also made clear that mental health must remain central to any decision. Reflecting on the demands of a possible return, she previously said: “Mental health plays a big role in it because, physically, my coaches will get me in shape. I can get myself in shape. We believe in that ability. We’re really thankful that I’m still healthy.”

Biles ' achievements at Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 have already secured her place among gymnastics' greatest athletes.

Her Paris comeback, after the difficulties she experienced in Tokyo, demonstrated that she can still perform at the highest level. But it does not mean she owes the sport another Olympic appearance.

For now, her public life appears centred on enjoying opportunities beyond competition, including supporting Owens , exploring fashion and spending time with the people closest to her.

Whether that reflects a deliberate break before training intensifies or a growing preference for life after gymnastics remains unknown.

The Los Angeles Games would offer Biles a rare chance to compete at an Olympics in her home country.

Yet until she shares a clearer commitment to training and makes a final decision, her return remains uncertain, and her busy life away from the gym is an increasingly prominent part of the story.

articles.title: Lindsey Vonn celebrates 42nd birthday with bold photos amid her Olympic recovery
articles.standfirst: The Olympic skiing legend marked another birthday with a series of eye-catching photos as she continues recovering from the devastating crash that derailed her 2026 Winter Games
articles.summary: The Olympic skiing legend marked another birthday with a series of eye-catching photos as she continues recovering from the devastating crash that derailed her 2026 Winter Games
articles.body:
Lindsey Vonn is celebrating her 42nd birthday with confidence, giving fans another glimpse of her personality away from the slopes as she continues to work through one of the most difficult recoveries of her sporting career.

The American skiing icon turned 42 on October 18, 2026, and she marked the occasion by sharing photos in swimwear and workout gear.

The images celebrate Vonn's athletic physique and public image, but her birthday also arrives at a significant moment in her life, with the former Olympic champion still facing a lengthy rehabilitation following her devastating crash at the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics in February.

Vonn has spent much of 2026 rebuilding her strength after suffering a serious leg injury at the Games.

Although her competitive future remains uncertain, she has continued making public appearances and discussing the challenges of recovery, showing that her ambitions extend beyond simply returning to the mountain.

The birthday photos offer a lighter moment in a year dominated by medical setbacks.

They also highlight the confidence that has been a recurring part of Vonn's public persona throughout her career, both during her years at the top of alpine skiing and since she returned to competition after initially retiring.

Vonn's remarkable comeback meets another major setback

Vonn's latest chapter has been particularly dramatic because she had already overcome significant obstacles to return to elite competition.

After retiring in 2019, she underwent partial knee replacement surgery and eventually decided to return to the World Cup circuit in late 2024.

The comeback quickly delivered results, including a second-place finish in super-G in March 2025 and a historic downhill victory at St. Moritz in December 2025, when she became the oldest woman to win a World Cup downhill race.

Those achievements helped her secure a place on the U.S. team for the 2026 Winter Olympics, making her fifth Olympic appearance.

However, the road to the Games had already taken a painful turn when she tore the anterior cruciate ligament in her left knee during a crash shortly before the Olympic downhill event.

Despite that injury, Vonn chose to compete in Italy. Her Olympic downhill race ended almost immediately when she crashed, suffering a complex fracture to her left leg that required emergency treatment and multiple operations.

The consequences were severe. Vonn underwent eight surgeries and spent an extended period using a wheelchair before progressing in her rehabilitation.

In an October interview with Fortune, she said she was still considering the possibility of another comeback, although she acknowledged the enormous physical challenge involved. She also expected to undergo ACL surgery in November, with a recovery period of around nine months.

A birthday that arrives with questions about her future

Vonn's birthday comes as she continues to weigh what the next stage of her skiing career might look like.

She has not ruled out returning to competition, but the severity of her injuries means any decision will depend on her recovery and whether she can regain the strength and stability required for elite downhill racing.

The 2026-27 U.S. Alpine Ski Team roster still includes Vonn, although her participation will depend on her rehabilitation progress.

Being named to the roster does not guarantee that she will compete this season, particularly with further surgery and months of recovery ahead.

Her career has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to return from setbacks that might have ended another athlete's ambitions. Vonn has won three Olympic medals, including downhill gold at the 2010 Vancouver Games, and accumulated 84 World Cup victories across a career that established her among the greatest alpine skiers of her generation.

For now, her focus is on healing rather than setting a firm return date. The birthday photographs provide a celebration of the athlete beyond her injuries, while her latest comments suggest that she has not entirely closed the door on racing again.

Vonn's 42nd year begins with difficult questions about what her body will allow her to do next.

Yet, as she celebrates her birthday, she remains a prominent figure in winter sports, with a legacy that stands regardless of whether another competitive comeback becomes possible.

articles.title: Lindsey Vonn smiling again after injury and poses topless to promote new project
articles.standfirst: The skiing legend has unveiled a striking new clothing campaign
articles.summary: The skiing legend has unveiled a striking new clothing campaign
articles.body:
A devastating injury might have forced Lindsey Vonn to reconsider her immediate plans, but the Olympic champion has instead continued expanding her career away from the slopes, unveiling a new collection for her luxury winter fashion brand.

Vonn , who turned 42 this month, shared several photographs promoting Vonn Collective, her clothing venture developed alongside HEAD Sportswear, as she continues recovering from the crash she suffered at February's Winter Olympics.

The campaign featured a series of carefully styled outfits, including a striking image in which she appeared topless, photographed from behind while wearing tan trousers.

Other photographs showed Vonn modeling a cropped vest and hoodie, alongside a fitted white outfit and snow boots.

The images offered another glimpse of how the former World Cup champion is combining her sporting experience with an increasingly prominent role in fashion and business.

Vonn Collective was developed to combine technical winter sports clothing with contemporary fashion, offering garments designed for use beyond traditional skiing environments.

Vonn has maintained an active role in the brand's development, serving as its founder and creative director while helping shape each new collection.

"For the mountain, the resort and the city… it's always a vibe," she wrote on Instagram while introducing the latest campaign.

"We are growing this line every year and as the founder and creative director I couldn't be more excited about our evolution."

The American also explained that feedback from customers had influenced improvements to the clothing range.

"From last season we have made changes and upgrades based on your feedback and are always open to more. I hope you love it," she added.

Her promotional photographs attracted positive reactions, with one follower commenting, "Love it girl!" while another wrote, "This line is fire."

Olympic champion reflects on injury and turning 42

The collection's release coincided with Vonn 's birthday celebrations, which included a European vacation and time spent relaxing by the beach.

However, the milestone also prompted the skiing legend to reflect on how her attitude toward aging has changed since her earlier years as a professional athlete.

"Age is a funny thing… my perspective of life at 30 was that (especially as an athlete) I was over the hill, but now that I'm in my 40's I feel the knowledge of life that I have amassed makes me feel somehow much younger and more confident in who I am," Vonn wrote.

Her comments came after a challenging year marked by the serious accident at the Winter Games and the recovery process that followed.

Vonn looks beyond skiing with growing business ambitions

Despite those difficulties, Vonn has continued sharing updates about her fitness activities, travels and entrepreneurial projects.

The Olympic champion also offered a personal message of gratitude while acknowledging the challenges she has encountered.

"Despite my crash and all of the things that have happened to me, the good, the bad the ugly… I'm always thankful to be in this life," she wrote. "Thankful for all the love and support I've received."

Alongside her clothing business, Vonn remains involved in philanthropy and investing, maintaining a professional presence well beyond competitive skiing.

Her latest campaign reflects that broader ambition, demonstrating how she continues drawing on her sporting background while exploring new opportunities in fashion.
